plan.curriculum: Mathematics 2.0, Number, Year 6 (VC2M6N09): mathematical modelling of a practical financial problem: formulating it, choosing operations, interpreting and justifying the solution in the situation
plan.shape: consolidation: one modelling cycle modelled by the teacher, then students carry out their own, because the week's skills come together in one task
plan.criticalFeature: say what the answer means in the situation, and justify the choices you made
decisionPoints: the choice check: which question needs answering first?
the hinge: is the plan within budget?
plan.anchor: read it, model it, solve it, check it: say what the answer means in the situation
plan.catchUp: Missed earlier sessions? Show the plan frame from Session 4 and one sale price before the launch.

studentTools: Printed Worksheet for every student; Extension and Supported Worksheet as needed
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
boardSetup: The fortnight's anchor on the board: read it, model it, solve it, check it
The party price list from the slides, written up for reference

resources.label: Worksheet
resources.description: Your turn. Plan an end-of-year party for 26 students with $150, using a price list with deals, and justify your choices.
resources.title: Modelling a Shopping Problem
resources.subtitle: Read it, model it, solve it, check it. Say what the answer means.

example.prompt: What do we find out first?

items.prompt: Read the price list. Answer the planning questions.

example.prompt: Cost of 3 pizzas with the deal?

items.prompt: Work out the cost of each item for the party.
The class wants a fruit platter ($22) too. What is the best change?
items.explain: With the platter the total is $169.10, $19.10 over. 3 fewer pizzas saves $39 ($130.10). 1 fewer cupcake box saves $15 and 1 fewer juice pack saves $7.20: not enough.

items.prompt: Ben added the juice cost. Find his mistake and fix it.

resources.label: Extension
resources.description: Early finisher option. More students, a delivery fee and a fundraising target, with worked examples.
resources.title: Extension: Change the Model
resources.subtitle: What if something changes?

example.prompt: If 4 more students come, what changes?

items.prompt: If 34 students come, how many juice packs and cupcake boxes are needed now? What does it add to the cost?
items.answer: 4 juice packs (+$7.20), 3 cupcake boxes (36 is enough): +$7.20

items.prompt: Each student eats 2 slices of pizza. Each pizza has 8 slices. How many pizzas for 34 students?

example.prompt: Delivery costs $9.95. Is the original plan still under $150?

items.prompt: With the $9.95 delivery fee, change the plan so it fits the $150 budget. Show the new total.
items.answer: For example: 5 pizzas (3 for $39 + 2 × $14.50 = $68), saving $10: total $147.05

example.prompt: The class sells cupcakes at $2 each. How many to raise $60?

items.prompt: The class wants $200 for next year's party. They sell drinks at $1.50 (cost 80c each). How many must they sell to make $200 profit? Show your model.
items.answer: Profit per drink: $0.70. $200 divided by $0.70 = 285.7..., so 286 drinks.

resources.title: Party Plan: Step by Step
resources.subtitle: One item at a time, then add.

items.prompt: How much is left from $100 after spending $83?

slides.notes: Session 5 of our money and percentages fortnight: today we model a whole shopping problem, start to finish.
Before you start, put boards and markers on every desk, and write the party price list on the board. Print the Worksheet for everyone, and a few copies of the Extension and the Supported Worksheet.

slides.title: Read the graph
prompts: How many more chose pizza than sushi?

beats: SAY: Let's warm up with statistics.
ASK: How many more students chose pizza than sushi?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 9
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> lay a ruler across each column top, read the scale, then subtract. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Pizza 14, sushi 5, so 9 more chose pizza. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 14, the pizza value.
Fix: ask what 'how many more' means, and they subtract.
notes.prep: Review of Week 3 statistics (the request named the focus). Keep the review under 6 minutes.

slides.title: Fair question?
prompts: Is this survey question fair? 'Don't you think pizza is the best party food?'

beats: ASK: Is this survey question fair? Thumbs up for fair, down for not fair.
10 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: thumbs down: it pushes towards yes
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> underline the pushing words together. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Not fair: 'Don't you think' pushes people to say yes.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: thumbs up.
Fix: read it aloud and listen for the push, and they decide again.

slides.title: Which display?
prompts: Which display suits 'votes for party food'?

beats: ASK: Which display suits votes for party food?
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: a column graph
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then on to Fluency.
Less -> ask: categories, a few numbers, or change over time? Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: A column graph: the foods are categories. Tick it or fix it.
trap: choosing a line graph.
Fix: ask whether the votes change over time, and they choose again.

slides.title: Divide with the division bracket: 3 digits

beats: SAY: Now for some short division with the division bracket.
Divide each digit from the left, and carry any remainder across.
ASK: Use the division bracket to solve this one.
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 106
SCAN boards for each digit of the answer.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> model the first column together on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The answer is 106.
Tick it or fix it, and check every step.
trap: leaving out a zero in the answer when a digit is too small to share.
Fix: ask "How many times does it go?", write 0, and they carry on.
notes.prep: Division fluency: 3 digits, then 4, then 5. Keep the whole block under 6 minutes.

slides.title: Divide with the division bracket: 4 digits

beats: SAY: Now it's 4 digits.
It's the same method, just one more column.
ASK: Use the division bracket to solve this one.
45 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 1 248
SCAN boards for each digit of the answer.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> model the first column together on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The answer is 1 248.
Tick it or fix it, and check every step.
trap: leaving out a zero in the answer when a digit is too small to share.
Fix: ask "How many times does it go?", write 0, and they carry on.

slides.title: Divide with the division bracket: 5 digits

beats: SAY: Now it's 5 digits.
It's the same method, just one more column.
ASK: Use the division bracket to solve this one.
60 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 5 225
SCAN boards for each digit of the answer.
80%+ -> reveal, then the learning intention.
Less -> model the first column together on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The answer is 5 225.
Tick it or fix it, and check every step.
trap: leaving out a zero in the answer when a digit is too small to share.
Fix: ask "How many times does it go?", write 0, and they carry on.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to model a real shopping problem and justify our choices.
successCriteria: I can work out what a problem is asking and plan the steps.
I can use discounts and deals to cost a plan within a budget.
I can explain what my answer means and justify my choices.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: This fortnight we've learned sales, best buys, GST and multi-step problems.
Today we use all of it in one real problem.
SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one is where we start,
and the second one is our big goal today.
notes.prep: SC1 planning is reachable for everyone; SC2 costing within a budget is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 justifying is the stretch.

slides.title: The end-of-year party
lines: Food and a drink for everyone.

notes.answer: how much, what cost, within budget?
beats: POINT to each line.
SAY: Our task today: plan the end-of-year party for 26 students with 150 dollars.
ASK: What questions do we need to answer before we can spend anything?
Tell your partner.
30 sec. Cue: Partner A first. You have 20 seconds. Go.
EXPECT: how much food and drink, what it costs, whether it fits
SAY: Good questions: how much do we need,
what will it cost, and does it fit the budget?
That's modelling: read it, model it, solve it, check it.
trap: starting to add prices straight away.
Fix: ask what we need to know first, and they plan.
notes.prep: The launch comes after the LI: the modelling task is posed before any numbers. Under 4 minutes.

slides.meaning: A plan for how much money you can spend, and what you will spend it on.

beats: POINT to the word.
SAY: This word is budget. Say it with me: bud-get.
SAY: A budget is a plan for how much money you can spend,
and what you'll spend it on.
Staying within budget means not spending more than you have.
ASK: If the budget is $150 and we spend $147.10, are we within budget?
10 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up
trap: thinking any amount near $150 is fine.
Fix: compare the numbers, and they check again.
notes.prep: Budget leads into next week's earning and saving.

slides.title: Model it
steps: Model: 6 pizzas, 3 juice packs, 3 cupcake boxes, plates.

beats: MODEL choosing amounts.
SAY: 26 students need about 6 pizzas,
3 juice packs and 3 boxes of cupcakes, plus plates.
MODEL the costs with deals.
SAY: 6 pizzas is two lots of the 3 for 39 deal: 78.
Juice is 24 less 10 percent: 21.60.
Cupcakes: 2 boxes for 26, plus 15. Plates are 6.50.
ASK: What is the total, and is it within budget?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: $147.10, yes
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 147.10, so we're within budget with 2.90 left.
Now I'd tell the principal why this plan works.
trap: forgetting a deal.
Fix: reread the deal column, and they recost.
notes.stretch: Could we afford a fruit platter too? What would change?
notes.help: Cost one item at a time in a table.
notes.prep: The full modelling cycle, modelled once. SC1 to SC3.

slides.title: What comes first?
slides.prompt: Point to A, B or C

options.text: Add up every price on the list.
options.misconception: calculates before deciding what is needed

options.text: Decide how much food and drink 26 students need.
Take $150 away from the most expensive item.
options.misconception: picks an operation without a plan

beats: SAY: We're planning the party. What do we do first?
ASK: Which step comes first?
15 sec. Cue: Voices off. Point... now. Hold your point.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then cold call one student: What comes second?
Less -> go back to the plan frame: know, need, steps. Re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: It's B. We can't cost anything until we know how much we need.
Adding every price doesn't answer the question.
trap: pointing to A.
Fix: ask what adding every price tells us, and they choose again.
notes.prep: First decision point: formulating before calculating.

slides.title: Cost it
slides.pivot: check the deal column, then calculate one item at a time
slides.followUp: cold call one board: Did you use a deal? Which one?

say: Write each cost on your board.
trap: missing a deal.
Fix: reread the deal column, and they recost.
notes.stretch: Find the cheapest way to buy 5 pizzas.
notes.help: Use the price list on the board.
notes.prep: Guided practice costing items with and without deals. SC2.

beats: SAY: This one is just for you.
The budget here is 100 dollars.
ASK: Is this plan within a $100 budget? By how much over or under?
40 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: no, $7.90 over
SCAN every board, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then Your turn.
Less -> add two costs at a time together. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The total is 107.90, so it's 7.90 over budget.
We'd need to change something. Tick it or fix it.
trap: saying it fits.
Fix: add the costs again and compare with $100, and they decide again.
notes.prep: The hinge before independent work. Anyone who says it fits starts on the Supported Worksheet with the teacher.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: Plan the party on your worksheet, then justify your plan.

beats: POINT to the steps.
SAY: Read each question carefully, solve it carefully, then check your answers.
SAY: If you finish, the Extension is your early finisher option.
Let's read the steps together. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE and ask: What does your total mean for the party?
TIME: 20 minutes. Stop everyone once at 10 minutes to share a strategy.
trap: a total with no decision.
Fix: ask whether it fits the budget, and they say so.
notes.stretch: Extension: more students, a delivery fee and fundraising.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: whole-dollar prices, one item at a time.
notes.prep: Independent practice: the full modelling cycle with deals and a justification. The sheet is evidence for SC2 and SC3.

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: Can the class afford 5 pizzas and 3 juice packs with $90? Explain.

visual.text: At another shop, pizza is $13 each or 3 for $36. Juice is $9 a pack, with 10% off.

beats: SAY: Here's the last one. Work it out on your own board.
ASK: Can the class afford 5 pizzas and 3 juice packs with 90 dollars? Explain.
60 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
RECORD who ignores a deal or gives no decision.
Their names go to next week's budgeting group.
trap: saying no, without the deal.
Fix: none now. Record the name for tomorrow.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2 and SC3: cost a new plan with deals and decide.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Tell your partner one choice you made in your party plan, and why.

notes.answer: open - listen for a choice with a money reason
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you that you can model a money problem and justify it?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit board.
A thumb up with 'no' on the exit board matters most.
ASK: What is one choice you made in your plan, and why?
20 sec. Cue: Partner B first. You have 20 seconds. Go.
EXPECT: a choice with a money reason
notes.prep: Fortnight midpoint: next week is earning, saving and budgeting.
